title: Kumara Roesti
description: A Chef Aly Thermomix reinterpretation of a Sean Connolly-style kumara roesti: golden, crisp-edged potato and kumara cakes with fresh herbs and a hint of spice, using precise TM6 and TM7 settings for the perfect crunch.
intro: This is my independent Thermomix homage to Sean Connolly and the satisfying crunch of a golden kumara roesti. The Thermomix grates the kumara and potato in seconds, then you pan-fry spoonfuls until they're crisp outside and tender within — a brilliant NZ café classic made easy at home.
ingredients: Lemon wedges and sour cream, to serve
steps: Grate the kumara and potato 5 sec / speed 5. Transfer to a clean tea towel and squeeze out as much liquid as possible. Set aside in a large bowl.
Chop the onion 3 sec / speed 5. Add to the bowl with the grated kumara and potato.
Add the eggs, flour, parmesan, smoked paprika, chives, thyme, salt and pepper to the bowl with the kumara mixture. Combine 8 sec / Reverse / speed 3 until evenly mixed.
Heat 5 mm of oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Spoon ¼-cup portions of the mixture into the pan, flattening gently with a spatula.
Cook for 3–4 minutes each side until deeply golden and crisp. Drain on paper towel. (Pan finish.)
Serve immediately with lemon wedges and a dollop of sour cream.
tips: Squeezing the moisture out of the grated kumara and potato is the key to crisp, not soggy, roesti.
Don't overcrowd the pan — cook in batches so they crisp properly.
The smoked paprika adds a subtle smoky note that pairs beautifully with the natural sweetness of kumara.

faq.q: Is this the original Sean Connolly recipe?
faq.a: No. This is Chef Aly's independent Thermomix reinterpretation inspired by Sean Connolly and kumara roesti; it is not endorsed by or affiliated with the chef.
You can grate and squeeze the kumara and potato up to 2 hours ahead, kept in the fridge. Cook fresh for the best crunch.
